sources.title: Functional Errata / Relevant Functional Errata - EdisonFormat.com
sources.used_for: The Edison community's explicit per-card list of cards errata'd after 2010 whose 2010-era behaviour differs from the modern text, plus the period rulings corpus (Individual Card Rulings posts) documenting the era's failed-search Deck/hand verification card by card. Used as independent corroboration of functional/ruling classifications - e.g. Sangan (the searched monster's effects were usable), Rescue Cat (no negation, no once-per-name), Catapult Turtle / Brionac / Treeborn Frog / Destiny End Dragoon (no once-per-turn), Necrovalley (negation applied only to effects targeting in a Graveyard), Darkness Approaches (face-down ATTACK position), Goyo Guardian (non-EARTH Tuners legal as material), Union monsters (the one-Union-per-monster Condition, removed by later errata).
sources.reliability_notes: Community secondary source; the blog version (2020-07-01) cites Konami tournament-policy section IX.G as the reason post-2010 errata text governs sanctioned play, which is why the site documents the era behaviour separately. It corroborates behaviour, not chronology: the page dates nothing, so effective dates are anchored to printings or to primary rulings documents instead.

sources.title: Upper Deck Entertainment official Yu-Gi-Oh! Card Rulings pages (Internet Archive captures, 2005-2009)
sources.notes: UDE's per-card rulings database, the ruling layer in force in the GOAT era. The 2005-06-16 capture (inside the April-October 2005 GOAT window) states the failed-search verification procedure verbatim for Sangan and Witch of the Black Forest: 'If you have no eligible monsters, your opponent gets to see your Deck to verify.' Reinforcement of the Army's entry then permitted activation with no valid target subject to the same verification; by the 2008-12-15 yugioh-card.com Card FAQ capture that had changed to 'You cannot activate ... if you do not have any Level 4 or lower Warrior-Type monsters remaining in your Deck' - per-card activation-condition chronology differs from the shared verification chronology. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Konami per-set Card Rulings documents, 2010-2011 (yugioh-card.com, Internet Archive)
sources.notes: Konami's official rulings documents for the Konami era. 'Machina Mayhem Structure Deck - Card Rulings, Compiled as of April 6th, 2010' - eighteen days before the Edison snapshot - applies failed-search verification twice ('If you do not have "Commander Covington" in your Deck, your opponent can ask to verify'). Starstrike Blast (2010-11-16) extends it to the Extra Deck and Storm of Ragnarok (2011-02-02) to the hand; 2011-02-02 is the latest date the old state is positively attested. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Konami Digital Entertainment Official Tournament Policy - 'Card/Hand/Deck Verification' (archived, 2019-2025)
sources.notes: The modern state: KDE tournament policy forbids searching or verifying an opponent's Deck outside specific cases, using a failed Mystic Tomato search as its worked example. First located capture 2019-04-03; unchanged in KDE-US Tournament Policy v2.5 (in effect 2025-09-05). The KDE policy documents in force in April 2010 (Tournament Policy v1.0 valid 2010-02-01, Penalty Guidelines valid 2010-04-01) contain no failure-to-find clause at all - in that era the rule lived in the rulings layer, not policy. No dated announcement of the change was found: the transition interval 2011-02-02 .. 2019-04-03 remains open. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Format Library source repository (danielmcnelis/formatlibrary)
sources.notes: Nx monorepo behind formatlibrary.com. Inspected for its errata data model: libs/models/src/lib/Errata.js defines an 'erratas' table (cardName, cardId, description, effectiveDate, expirationDate, isOriginal, isActive) that no route, script or UI reads - schema-only. Period card texts actually live per printing in Print.description (populated by a Feb 2024 Yugipedia scrape) and are deliberately excluded from the card API response; the site-wide Card.description is the CURRENT text synced nightly from YGOPRODeck. Format-specific behaviour is carried by human-written Ruling rows keyed to a format, not by machine-readable period text. Retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Upper Deck Entertainment 'Card Text Updates / Errata & Card Text FAQ's' page (Internet Archive captures)
sources.notes: UDE's official running list of TCG card-text corrections and updated texts, per card with the affected printings. A capture attests the OFFICIAL text as of the capture date, which bounds text-change chronology in the UDE era; Yugipedia's Card Errata pages cite this page for several UDE-announced errata (e.g. the XYZ union monsters). Local copy of the 2009-02-20 capture in the research cache; retrieved 2026-08-20.

sources.title: Yugipedia Card Errata pages (Card Errata: namespace, per-language {{Errata table}} text lineages)
sources.notes: One structured page per errata'd card: successive card texts with diff markup, each captioned with the printing (set + number) exemplifying that version. Fetched via the MediaWiki API by retroformats/importers/fetch_errata_sources.py (batched revisions queries, 1 req/s, descriptive UA); page revision ids are stamped into the research packets. Used for text lineages and for bounding when a new text was first available in the TCG (the introducing printing's set release date); wording is community-transcribed, so functional-vs-cosmetic judgements also cross-check the pinned BabelCDB texts.

sources.title: Yugipedia set pages (Semantic MediaWiki release-date properties, per territory)
sources.notes: Queried per the published API policy (1 req/s, descriptive UA, cached). Exact queries, retrieval dates, and page counts are stamped into data/imported/releases-report.json by the importer. Date precision parsed from SMW raw values (1/YYYY[/M[/D]]), never from padded timestamps.

sources.title: YGOPRODeck API v7 bulk dumps (cardinfo.php?misc=yes, cardsets.php)
sources.notes: Single-request bulk download per their stated caching mandate. Printings/identity authority only: its per-set tcg_date is region-inconsistent (verified EU for some sets, NA for others), so it corroborates or falls back, never overrides Yugipedia dates. Retrieval stamped in data/imported/releases-report.json.

sources.title: Konami premier-event card-legality FAQs 2009-2010 (US Nationals 2009, Regionals, 2010 US WCQ; archived) and the 2010-03-19 Duel Terminal legality article
sources.notes: Konami-era legality practice: per-event dated legal lists. Evidence that Europe-only GX Tag Force 3 promos (Gallis the Star Beast, Red-Eyes Wyvern, Darkness Destroyer) were explicitly legal at US premier events 2009-2010, and that Duel Terminal machine-exclusive cards were NOT legal until released in another product (mid-2009 FAQs naming Ally of Justice Catastor; Kevin Tewart's 2010-03-19 strategy-site article; the June 2010 US WCQ FAQ enumerating still-illegal DT01/DT02 numbers). Local copies cached; retrieved 2026-08-20.
